newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks head higher again at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks head higher again at open.

text.p: The Australian share market headed higher again at the open on Thursday with enthusiastic local investors taking a lead from another surge on Wall Street.
The All Ordinaries index added 12.0 points to a record high of 2,757.9, surpassing the previous record 2,751.4 reached on Wednesday.
"There is no doubt it's a strong market," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank, citing a bank sector that again outperformed the broader market.
"The banks are doing more than their share but Hills (BHP) have done a bit as well."

Sector leader National Australia Bank, up 15 cents to A$19.54 (US$14.66), and Westpac Banking Corporation, up nine cents to A$8.06, were the best of them. Besides the ever popular yield argument for these stocks, speculation is mounting that Westpac's bid for the Victorian-based regional Bank of Melbourne will soon get the regulatory go-ahead.
Bellwether BHP was up 11 cents at A$19.94, while Rio Tinto lost 17 cents to A$22.80 after sliding in London.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 40 percent of stocks traded reamined steady.
